draft.title: The business cycle
card: The business cycle is the pattern in which real GDP rises and falls around its long-term trend. Real GDP is output adjusted for price changes.
a period when real GDP is growing. It continues until it reaches a peak, often called a boom, when growth is strong and output is high.
a period when growth in real GDP slows or output falls. A recession is a more serious downswing, often defined as two or more quarters in a row of falling real GDP.
The cycle is not regular. The length and size of upswings and downswings vary, and the economy moves around the trend instead of staying on it.
draft.remember: The economy swings around its long-term trend: upswings, booms, downswings and recessions.

a.q: Real GDP in Country Y falls for the third quarter in a row. Which phase is it in?
opts: A recession
A boom
An upswing
The long-term trend
a.why: Real GDP has fallen for more than two quarters in a row, which fits a recession. A boom is a time of strong growth, so it is the opposite.
a.clue: Count how many quarters in a row real GDP has fallen.

b.q: Real GDP in Country Z keeps growing, but the growth rate drops from 4% to 1%. Which statement is correct?
opts: It is in a downswing, as growth has slowed
It is in a recession, as growth has fallen
It is in a boom, as real GDP is still rising
It is in an upswing, as real GDP is still rising
b.why: The card says a downswing is when growth slows or output falls, so slowing growth fits. It is not a recession, as real GDP has not fallen for two quarters in a row.
b.clue: A downswing can include slower growth, not only falling output.

b.best: It is in a downswing, as growth has slowed
also_right: It is in an upswing, as real GDP is still rising

proposal.title: The business cycle
card: The business cycle is the pattern in which real GDP rises and falls around its long-term trend. Real GDP is output adjusted for price changes.
a period when the growth rate of real GDP is rising or staying strong. It leads to a peak, often called a boom, when growth is fast and output is high.
a period when the growth rate of real GDP slows, or output falls. A recession is a more serious downswing, often defined as two or more quarters in a row of falling real GDP.
The cycle is not regular. The length and size of upswings and downswings vary, and the economy moves around the trend instead of staying on it.
proposal.remember: Watch the growth rate: rising or strong growth is an upswing, slowing growth or falling output is a downswing.

a.q: Real GDP in Country Y falls for the third quarter in a row. Which phase is it in?
opts: A recession
A boom
An upswing
The long-term trend
a.why: Real GDP has fallen for more than two quarters in a row, which fits a recession. A boom is a time of fast growth and high output, so it is the opposite.
a.clue: Count how many quarters in a row real GDP has fallen.

b.q: Real GDP in Country Z keeps growing, but the growth rate drops from 4% to 1%. Which statement is correct?
opts: It is in a downswing, as the growth rate has slowed
It is in a recession, as the growth rate has fallen
It is in a boom, as real GDP is still rising
It is in an upswing, as real GDP is still rising
b.why: A downswing is when the growth rate slows or output falls, and here the growth rate has slowed from 4% to 1%. It is not an upswing, because that needs the growth rate to be rising or staying strong. It is not a recession, as real GDP has not fallen at all.
b.clue: Look at what the growth rate is doing, not just whether output rose.
